summary: Bonner County cabin, not a tower, near Blanchard at 2,900 feet: built in 1935, abandoned in 1939 and gone. A 1927 report mentions a Blanchard lookout line; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: The cabin was abandoned in 1939 and is gone; no source describes what, if anything, remains at the site.

events.note: A January 1927 fire warden's report, quoted on the Forest Lookouts site, mentions a Blanchard lookout line and a repeating coil; no source says what stood on the site then
Cabin, per all three lookout pages

evidence.supports: two miles north of Blanchard, Bonner County

evidence.quote: We don't yet have a documented staffing history for this lookout.

evidence.supports: 1927 fire warden's report mentions the Blanchard lookout line and repeating coil
evidence.quote: A repeating coil was placed at the tie-in of the Blanchard lookout line.

evidence.supports: the coil let the lookout reach head office and the wardens at Priest River
evidence.quote: This enables the lookout to communicate with head office and the resident wardens at Priest River also.

evidence.supports: January 1927 fire warden's report quoted on the Forest Lookouts site

sources.title: Twenty-Fourth and Twenty-Fifth Annual Reports of the Pend d'Oreille Timber Protective Association
sources.publisher: University of Idaho Library Digital Collections

resolved_conflicts.explanation: All three lookout pages date the cabin to 1935, so 1935 is kept. The 1927 fire warden's report mentions a Blanchard lookout line but does not say a cabin stood there; the earlier date is noted, not resolved.

notes_for_editor: Record checked: ground kind, gone status and coordinates match the Idaho list. Record events list only 1939 abandoned; the 1935 cabin date is added from all three lookout pages. The 1927 Blanchard lookout line is unexplained: a human could check the Idaho TPA annual reports for what stood there. A Facebook group search result mentions a two-storey 14 by 14 foot cabin one mile southwest of Blanchard at 2,858 feet, which may be a different structure; it was not read or cited. Access is left out of facts because no source says whether the site is public today.
